newsitem.title: FRANCE: Libyan envoy arrives in Algeria, slams Euro-force.
newsitem.headline: Libyan envoy arrives in Algeria, slams Euro-force.

text.p: A Libyan minister responsible for relations with neighbouring Maghreb countries arrived in Algeria on Wednesday and condemned a rapid intervention force set up last week by four European countries.

Algeria's official news agency APS said Libya's Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani said on arrival that his country rejected the force, known as Eurofor, set up by France, Italy, Spain and Portugal for use on humanitarian and peacekeeping missions.
Fezzani said Libya believed "this initiative represents a danger and menace for the security, sovereignty and independence of the countries of the Arab Maghreb Union" .
The union consists of Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia.
Fezzani said he would discuss with Algerians the latest developments facing the union and ways to face them.
APS said the Libyan envoy later met Algerian President Liamine Zeroual for whom he had a letter from Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.
On Monday, Gaddafi condemned the formation of Eurofor and termed the move "a step to break all the good relations between Arab and European countries."
He added: "Libya will probably begin to prepare a force to resist the European forces."

Libyan television earlier reported that Tripoli had warned Italy, France, Spain and Portugal that it would retaliate against the force by helping the Irish Republican Army (IRA) in Britain and similar groups in other European countries.
